mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 4.0% consistently precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to accommodative monetary policy reducing the discount rate for equity valuation.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window, or 20-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) when FEDFUNDS < 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 205.0 indicates accelerating inflation, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as central banks respond with rate hikes.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 205.0, or the signal's Rank IC is negative over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and payroll employment (PAYEMS) from their 3-month averages signal labor market overheating, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to imminent monetary tightening.
failure_condition: The joint decline condition occurs but SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of cases, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Strong housing market activity (HOUST > 1800) during expansionary regimes correlates with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as housing signals consumer confidence and spending strength.
failure_condition: HOUST > 1800 but SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances, or the correlation coefficient is below 0.1.

mechanism_narrative: A manufacturing production index (INDPRO) above 115.0 indicates robust industrial output, typically leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as it reflects economic expansion.
failure_condition: INDPRO > 115.0 but SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of cases, or the signal's Rank IC is negative.

mechanism_narrative: In tight labor market regimes (UNRATE < 4.0%), the S&P 500 exhibits positive 20-day returns due to sustained wage growth and consumer spending, but this effect reverses when unemployment rises above 4.0%.
failure_condition: UNRATE < 4.0% but SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances, or the return difference between tight and loose labor markets is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A retail sales figure (RSAFS) below 360,000 million dollars signals weak consumer spending, associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced economic activity.
failure_condition: RSAFS < 360000 but SPX 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances, or the signal's Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 5.0% over the prior month triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to immediate market reaction to rate hikes.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 5.0 but SPX 5-day returns are positive in > 60% of instances, or the signal's Rank IC is negative.
